analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata. ProviderLoop.swift:705–716 adds recovery state, an internal load override and saved enabled-model snapshots; :868 initializes the saved filter without changing the visible serving selection or inventory eligibility checks. ProviderLoop+Testing.swift:514–522 exposes internal recovery test hooks, consistent with existing internal seams; no external invocation path is shown. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:50–54 adds model-filter and recovery diagnostics to the existing local daemon-state writer (:26–29). The additions do not visibly persist prompts, private keys or tokens, change authorization handling (:147–169), or alter encryption, cache scoping, billing or privileged fan control. No concrete security regression is established in this scope.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryReport(), DaemonState serialization and recovery call sites: bounded retries and memory admission, cancellation/shutdown, selection changes during an await, and whether recovered slots retain weight verification and cache bindings. These contracts are outside the supplied source, not observed missing controls. They are material to availability (T-010/T-029), model integrity (T-012/T-027), cache isolation (T-041), and connection-bound serving authorization (T-052/T-053). Confirm recovery diagnostics contain only operational metadata (T-058) and never function as authorization. Only indexed summaries and selected threat details were supplied; this local pass does not establish the security of the recovery implementation or unchanged callers.
